name: addons-ios
description: iOS, behaviorally parallel to the proven test-cases/addons.json (Android), authored from the same plain-language narrative (login -> dismiss post-login dialogs/tutorial -> view Add-ons -> log out). test-cases/addons.json's resolvedSelector/selector/expect values are Android-specific (UiAutomator2 xpath, Android resource-ids, Android's permissioncontroller package) and do not apply on iOS's XCUITest tree, so none of them are carried over or guessed at here -- every step relies on instruction text for Phoenix's semantic-resolution layer (generation/semantic-act.js) to resolve at runtime against the real iOS element tree. RUN 1 (addons-run-ios-docker-1.log, real MyYes_19.3.11.ipa on BrowserStack App Automate, iPhone 15/iOS): FAILED at the original step 0 -- 'snapshot does not contain any element labeled LOGIN button' -- because iOS shows its native notification-permission alert immediately on first launch, before login, unlike Android where the equivalent dialog appears post-login (addons.json steps 8-9). Fixed by adding a new optional dismiss-notification-dialog step at index 0, ahead of the login attempt, from that real evidence. RUN 2 (addons-run-ios-docker-2.log): bug #1's fix was never actually exercised to a verdict -- the run failed on the very next step, 'tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form', with the resolver declining and reporting that the only 'LOGIN'-named elements belonged to an unrelated 'Login More Menu New' button. The real captured page-source XML proved a plain, visible, accessible, genuinely unambiguous LOGIN button WAS present and unrelated to that other button -- the bug was in generation/semantic-snapshot.js's buildGroundedSnapshot(): iOS nests a StaticText with the identical name INSIDE the button it labels (one visual control, represented twice in the tree), and the ambiguousAccessibilityId check counted that nested StaticText as a second, independently-tappable duplicate, falsely flagging the LOGIN button (and every other labeled button on this screen -- EN, ACTIVATE SIM) as ambiguous. Fixed by only treating two same-named elements as genuinely ambiguous when neither is an ancestor/descendant of the other, so a button and its own label child no longer falsely trigger each other while two real, unrelated same-named controls (the original home-LOGIN-vs-submit-LOGIN case this flag was built for) still do. RUN 3 (addons-run-ios-docker-3.log): bug #2's fix worked -- LOGIN resolved and clicked, the phone number was typed -- but the run failed one step later on 'tap the PASSWORD tab to switch the form into password-entry mode', with the resolver declining: 'no element on the screen has this label or role'. Investigated by feeding this run's real captured XML into buildGroundedSnapshot() directly: the PASSWORD button (same nested-button-with-matching-StaticText-child shape as the LOGIN bug) IS present, correctly unambiguous, not filtered as a dead end, and resolves to a normal accessibility-id selector -- it reaches the model-facing candidate list completely intact. No code-level defect was found; this is concluded to be a model/prompting-level issue (the local Ollama model declining a correct, unambiguous match, plausibly over the instruction's word 'tab' vs. the candidate's rendered role 'Button'), not a snapshot-building or resolution-engine bug, so the step wording and resolution code were left unchanged. A regression test pinning down the code-level finding was still added. test-cases/addons.ios.json has still not had a fully clean run -- steps through phone-number entry now have real evidence behind them, but the PASSWORD-tab step and everything after it (password entry, submit, tutorial carousel, Add-ons tab, logout) remain unverified/blocked pending a fix to the model-prompting side of this or a future run that gets past it.

steps.instruction: tap Allow or Don't Allow to dismiss the notification-permission system dialog if it's open
steps.note: REAL EVIDENCE, addons-run-ios-docker-1.log: on iOS this native alert ('"MyYes" Would Like to Send You Notifications', Allow/Don't Allow) appears immediately on first app launch, before login -- not after login as on Android (see addons.json steps 8-9, where the equivalent dismiss is positioned post-login). The alert covers the whole screen, so the very first run's step 0 ('tap the LOGIN button') failed with 'snapshot does not contain any element labeled LOGIN button' -- genuinely because the login button was hidden behind this dialog, not because the app failed to launch. Added here, before the login attempt, to match iOS's actual first-launch behavior.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
close the More-menu overlay if it's open (More Close icon)
steps.note: GUESS, iOS: mirrors addons.json step 1's Android More-menu-overlay recovery. No iOS evidence yet that this screen or control exists on iOS at all -- kept as a no-op-safe tapIfExists rather than dropped, same reasoning addons.json itself used before it had a confirmed selector.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
steps.note: Retry of the LOGIN tap, mirrors addons.json step 2 -- a no-op once the login form is already open.

steps.instruction: type the phone number into the phone/account number field
tap the PASSWORD tab to switch the form into password-entry mode
tap the password field to focus it
type the password into the password field
tap the LOGIN button to submit the login form
wait for the login submission to finish and any notification-permission dialog to appear
steps.note: Mirrors addons.json step 8's confirmed Android timing race (a variable-length spinner before the permission dialog renders). Kept as a precaution for iOS too -- unconfirmed whether the same race exists on iOS, but a fixed wait here is cheap and the Android evidence for needing one at this exact point in the flow is real.

steps.instruction: tap Allow to dismiss the notification-permission dialog if it's open
steps.note: iOS shows its own native 'App Would Like to Send You Notifications' alert with Allow/Don't Allow buttons (a system alert, not an in-app popup) -- different control from Android's permissioncontroller dialog, so addons.json's Android resource-id selector is not reused; left for semantic resolution since no real iOS alert hierarchy has been captured yet.
